scale.label: acceptable but not ready to progress

stages.name: Functional Stability
stages.definition: Athlete can hold clean positions and perform basic movement patterns with control.
stages.gate: Own basic position before speed, load or chaos.

stages.name: Maximum Stability
stages.definition: Athlete can maintain clean positions under perturbation, instability, fatigue or contact-like challenge.
stages.gate: Stay organized when stability is challenged.

stages.name: Strength Stabilization
stages.definition: Athlete can produce force while maintaining alignment and control.

stages.name: Maximum Strength
stages.definition: Athlete can produce high force without losing structure.

stages.name: Power
stages.gate: Fast force without losing Activate standards.

stages.name: Maximum Power
stages.definition: Athlete can repeatedly produce explosive outputs while preserving movement quality.

stages.name: Beast Mode
stages.definition: Repeated controlled violence with clean mechanics under fatigue, chaos, instability and contact-like demands.
stages.gate: High rugby power repeatedly without posture, balance, alignment or decision-making breakdown.

candidateRule: Each applicable approved dimension must be at least 4 (source label progression-ready); no averaging. Coach must document context, applicable dimensions, repeated observations and limitations. No fixed observation count or time window established.
excluded: contact and neck competency require separate approved protocol
approvalRequired: minimum observation count and time window
